answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to earn trust through repeated, stake-backed interactions with independently chosen peers: a newcomer deposits collateral, and its score rises only when diverse partners later attest that its work was useful. A fake identity farm cannot cheaply echo praise among hollow accounts, because correlated attestations are discounted and conflicting reports slash the deposit. The attacker must fund many identities and risk losing stake, driving expected profit toward nadir.
